endpoints.name: Summerville
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/185236364 power=substation substation=transmission voltage=230000;115000 (unnamed). HIFLD 113527 (SCE&G 230 kV, 22.9 km) runs from OSM way/184867924 'Williams Substation' to this sub.
endpoints.validation: This is DESC's 'Summerville 230kV Sub' (SCRTP 2024-28 05004 P) and the Summerville end of the 'Williams - Summerville 230 kV' line (SCRTP 6388 A). It is the only 230/115 kV transmission sub in Summerville, and HIFLD's 230 kV line from Williams ends here; I re-checked that geometry myself. Nominatim reverse puts it in Berkeley County, in the Summerwood part of Summerville. HIFLD shows 115 kV lines leaving it west and south into Dorchester County. The gazetteer's 'Summerville Substation' at 34.47,-85.34 is in Summerville, Georgia, a same-name false match that was correctly rejected. OSM has no name tag, so the ID rests on topology.

projects.notes: The point is the loop's source substation, not the work site. Dominion's page (desc-summerville-loop-page) describes about 8 miles of 115 kV wood-to-steel replacement in Dorchester County, starting fall 2025 and running to summer 2026. HIFLD shows the Summerville 115 kV lines running up to about 8 km west and southwest of this point (for example HIFLD 141505 to 32.984,-80.212).

endpoints.name: Columbia Canal
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/291364662 power=plant name='Columbia Canal Power Plant' operator='South Carolina Electric & Gas Co.' (OSM way/1078308089 'Columbia Canal Substation', 33 kV, is 80 m away)
endpoints.validation: The name matches, and the operator is SCE&G, now DESC. It is on the Columbia Canal in downtown Columbia, Richland County. The only 115 kV line along the canal is HIFLD 110438 (SCE&G 115 kV, 3.2 km). It runs from the 230/115/33 kV sub at 34.0216,-81.0603 (OSM way/185230443) south along the canal to a 115 kV sub at 34.0004,-81.0486 (OSM way/329102047), 0.3 km from this plant. That line fits the plan's 'poles on the Columbia side of the canal'.

projects.notes: The pole work runs along HIFLD 115 kV line 110438 beside the canal, from this point up to about 2.8 km north (34.022,-81.060). The point marks the south end at the canal hydro plant, not a line terminus.

endpoints.name: Scout (customer substation)
endpoints.coordinateSource: Site estimate, not a mapped feature. It sits inside the Scout Motors tract, west of I-77 (OSM way/172626836, about -80.982 at this latitude) and southeast of Blythewood Road (OSM way/714373391, which runs from 34.2136,-80.9892 to 34.1894,-81.0349). Bounds come from the Scout Motors FAQ (a buffer 'along Blythewood Road') and PSC Order 2024-357 p.3 (scpsc-2024-80-e-scout-order).
endpoints.validation: PSC Order 2024-357 p.3 says DESC will break the VCS1-Killian 230 kV line 'along Highway 21 near the existing Blythewood Switching Station', run it across I-77 and onto the Scout property with about 2.5 miles of new right-of-way, and 'carry the line in a westerly direction into the Scout Substation', on Richland County land leased to Scout. This point is 2.9 km (1.8 mi) from the VCS1-Killian line (HIFLD 148554), which fits a 2.5-mile routed fold-in. The earlier point (the west end of the OSM 'Scout Motors Spur' rail construction) sits on I-77 itself, only 1.4 km from the line, so it was moved 2.2 km west. The substation itself is not in OSM. A radius of 3 km covers the tract from I-77 to about -81.035.

projects.notes: The main construction is the Scout substation and the 230 kV fold-in near Blythewood (I-77 / Highway 21). 'Modify VCS1 and Killian terminals' is terminal work only at two existing subs. They are listed here and not as endpoints, because the map code (centerOf) averages the first two endpoints and would otherwise put the center 14 km from Scout. VCS1 = OSM way/185039621 'Virgil C. Summer Nuclear #1 Substation', 230 kV, 34.2960,-81.3149. Killian = unnamed 230/115 kV OSM way/185201670 at 34.1223,-80.9441 (HIFLD node 117539), which is the end of the V C Summer 230 kV line HIFLD 148554. Its HIFLD path to Wateree Station (137325 + 127629) is 34.5 mi, which matches SCRTP 6808 R 'Wateree - Killian 230 kV ... Length - 35 miles'. The 115 kV switching station at 34.1900,-80.9684 (OSM way/558947932), 0.14 km from the line, is probably 'Blythewood Switching Station', but it is unnamed. The PSC order expected completion by 2026-03-31, and the SCRTP in-service date is 5/31/2026.

endpoints.name: Eastover
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/478709848 power=substation substation=switching voltage=115000 (unnamed) = HIFLD node UNKNOWN120856. HIFLD 130675 (115 kV, 11.8 km) runs from here east to TAP142281, where Progress Energy 115 kV segments continue to Sumter.
endpoints.validation: The cached V.C. Summer FSAR Table 8.1-1, 'Transmission System Ties to Other Utilities' (nrc-vcsummer-fsar-ch8-rev22 p.10), lists a Duke Energy-Progress tie 'Eastover | Sumter | 115', which confirms both terminal names. In HIFLD, the only 115 kV line that leaves the DESC system toward Sumter starts at this DESC hub. The hub also has SCE&G 115 kV lines to the International Paper Eastover mill (HIFLD 146792), to Wateree (129112) and west (147010). It is 5 km east-northeast of Eastover town, next to the Sylvamo/IP mill, and about 1.6 km west of the Wateree River, consistent with a DESC section of about 1 mile. OSM has no name tag.

endpoints.name: Sumter (DEP)
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/185032893 power=substation name='Sumter Substation' substation=transmission (= HIFLD UNKNOWN120918)
endpoints.validation: The name matches, and the sub is in Sumter (Duke Energy Progress territory). HIFLD shows Progress Energy 115 kV lines (131345, 117730) and a 230 kV line to WATEREE STATION (130315) ending at this node. That matches the FSAR ties 'Eastover-Sumter 115' and 'Wateree-Sumter 230'.

projects.notes: Only the DESC section of about 1 mile is rebuilt, at the Eastover/Wateree River end. The Eastover-Sumter midpoint is about 15 km east of the actual work. The FSAR tie table confirms this is a DESC-DEP interconnection.

endpoints.name: Batesburg

endpoints.validation: The name and 115 kV voltage match, it is in Batesburg-Leesville (DESC territory), and it is the only Batesburg-named feature in the gazetteer. HIFLD 137226 starts here.

endpoints.name: Saluda County
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/1041743427 power=substation name='Saluda Substation' voltage=115000 (town of Saluda, Saluda County) = HIFLD node UNKNOWN117178
endpoints.validation: The HIFLD 115 kV path from Batesburg (137226, 20.05 km, plus 122587, 1.64 km, via TAP153163) ends at this sub and totals 13.48 mi, against the plan's 'Rebuild 13.5 miles of conductor'. I re-measured this myself. It is the only 115 kV terminal sub in the town of Saluda; the only other 115 kV feature within 6 km is an unnamed industrial tap. The OSM name is 'Saluda', not 'Saluda County', but the location and length agree. This is not Saluda Hydro, which is 50 km east.

endpoints.name: Dawson

This new 230 kV transmission sub is 0.2-0.5 km west of the Canadys-Church Creek and Canadys-Faber Place 230 kV lines, about 560 m (1,850 ft) from the existing 230 kV sub on the line (OSM way/1319701989, probably Pine Hill), and 0.5 km from Research Center Drive. endpoints.name: Okatie
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/498967280 power=substation voltage=230000 (unnamed), next to OSM way/1064022697 230 kV switching (32.33376,-81.03261). 'Existing Okatie Substation' is marked on the official Dominion map desc-riverport-route-map.
endpoints.validation: I checked the map myself. Calibrating the rendered Dominion selected-route map on the Jasper Substation star and the 2-mile scale bar (about 31 m/px at 80 dpi) puts the 'Existing Okatie Substation' star at about 32.335,-81.030, within 150-200 m of this OSM feature. The star is where the Jasper-Okatie #2 corridor meets the existing Dominion line, east of I-95 and US 17, northeast of Hardeeville in Jasper County. The Jasper-Yemassee 230 kV #1 line that the plan folds in passes here. The gazetteer has no Okatie-named feature. This is not Okatie village in Beaufort County (32.296,-80.945).

projects.notes: The name 'Okatie' does not mean the Okatie village/SC-170 area, which is about 8.5 km east. Do not use that town centroid.

endpoints.name: Jasper
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/185380597 power=substation name='Jasper Substation' voltage=230000 substation=generation, at OSM way/449466227 'Jasper Generating Plant' operator DESC
endpoints.validation: The name matches and the operator is DESC, in Jasper County, SC. The other 'Jasper Substation' hits in the gazetteer (Tennessee, 35.07,-85.61; Florida, 30.51,-82.94) are wrong-state false matches and were rejected. The cached Dominion page says the first 230 kV line 'begins at the Jasper Generating Plant and ends at the Okatie substation'.

endpoints.name: Okatie
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/498967280 (230 kV) and way/1064022697 (230 kV switching); Dominion map desc-riverport-route-map
endpoints.validation: Same Okatie substation as desc:0139 M,N, located from the official route map. The straight-line distance to Jasper is 9 km (5.7 mi), consistent with a 6.5-mile routed line.

endpoints.validation: Same Okatie substation as desc:0139 M,N.

endpoints.name: Riverport
endpoints.coordinateSource: Read off the official Dominion map desc-riverport-route-map, the 'Proposed Riverport Substation' star (calibrated on Jasper Substation and the 2-mile scale bar). My own independent reading was about 32.227,-81.092, about 250 m away.
endpoints.validation: The map marks a proposed Riverport site at the south end of the 'Okatie - Riverport 230 kV' corridor, south of Hardeeville near Purrysburg Rd / SC-170 in Jasper County, on the SC side of the Savannah River. The same map shows a 'Proposed Sherwood Substation' about 1.6 km north (about 32.239,-81.095) on the same corridor. SCRTP 2024-28 (p.22) called project 06367 A-C,H 'Riverport Tap' ('Construct Okatie – Riverport 230 kV to feed new Distribution substation'). SCRTP 2025-29 (p.17) renamed the same ID 'Sherwood Tap' (Okatie – Sherwood 230 kV). The current Dominion page says the second line ends at Sherwood. So the terminus may be Sherwood; both sites are within the 2 km radius.

projects.notes: The SCRTP title says 115kV, but the description, the route map and the Dominion page all describe the Okatie-Riverport line as 230 kV. The line is about 8 miles and runs past Hardeeville. The Riverport end is about 10 km across the Savannah River from GPC's Savannah-area (zone 219) system, so it is a likely proximity candidate.

endpoints.name: Flat Rock
endpoints.coordinateSource: Midpoint of the tapped Belvedere Sw Sta - Graniteville 115 kV line (HIFLD 137404, 16.7 km; all vertices within 7.9 km of this point). The parallel Belvedere-Graniteville path, HIFLD 103497 via node 117192, is also entirely within 8.0 km.
endpoints.validation: The plan says the new sub is fed by a tap off the 'Belv Sw Sta - Graniteville 115 kV #1' line, so it must lie along that corridor between North Augusta and Graniteville in Aiken County, SC. HIFLD has two parallel 115 kV paths between the same hubs and it is unclear which one is '#1', but both are covered by the 8 km radius. No Flat Rock substation turned up in SC in OSM or on the web. The gazetteer's 'Flat Rock Substation' at 32.55,-84.87 is in Georgia, a false match. Flat Rock Pond and Flat Rock Lane in Graniteville (Nominatim, about 33.585-33.594,-81.81 to -81.83), 7.6 km northeast, are possible namesakes near the Graniteville end, but that is not confirmed.

projects.notes: The substation site is unresolved; use this locality (±8 km). The tapped line's terminals are context only, since no work is stated at them, so they are not listed as endpoints: Belvedere Sw Sta = unnamed 115 kV switching station, OSM way/1008277213 (33.5057,-81.9404, HIFLD hub 117199, North Augusta), and Graniteville = OSM relation/14294792 'Graniteville Substation' (33.5834,-81.8045). The area is about 10-25 km from Augusta, GA.

endpoints.name: Saluda Hydro
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/186840913 power=plant name='Saluda Hydroelectric Plant' operator='Dominion Energy South Carolina' (6065 Bush River Road). The 230/115 kV switchyard where HIFLD 133140 starts (OSM way/185149204, 34.05304,-81.20935) is 0.7 km east.
endpoints.validation: The name matches and the operator is DESC, at the Lake Murray dam. HIFLD names the node 'SALUDA LEXINGTON'. The cached FSAR tie table lists 'Saluda Hydro #1' and 'Saluda Hydro #2' as the DESC terminals of these tie lines.

endpoints.name: Bush River
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/185168619 power=substation substation=transmission voltage=230000;100000;44000 (unnamed) = HIFLD node UNKNOWN116988 (34.25246,-81.64871), Newberry County. This is Duke Energy Carolinas' Bush River Tie.
endpoints.validation: This is Duke Energy Carolinas' Bush River Tie, not a DESC sub. The cached V.C. Summer FSAR Table 8.1-1 (p.10) lists Duke Energy-Carolinas ties 'Saluda Hydro #2 | Bush River (W) | 115', 'Saluda Hydro #1 | Bush River (B) | 115' and 'VCS2 | Bush River | 230'. The cached SERTP 2025 plan names 'BUSH RIVER TIE 115/100 KV AUTOTRANSFORMERS' (p.30) and the 'Bush River Tie – Buzzard Roost 100 kV' line (p.33). In HIFLD, node 116988 is the only node with all of these: a Duke 100 kV line to BUZZARD ROOST (126116), a Duke 230 kV line to the V.C. Summer 2/3 switching station (135934, ending at OSM way/552845047), and two 115 kV lines from the Saluda/Chapin direction (168312 and 118261). The 115 kV path runs 133140 → 167351 → 168312 from the Saluda Hydro switchyard. The new cached Dominion 'Saluda-Bush River' page (desc-saluda-bushriver-page) puts the rebuild in 'Lexington, Newberry and Richland counties' and 'between the Ballentine and Little Mountain communities'. HIFLD 133140 passes 2.3 km from Ballentine and 1.9 km from Little Mountain on its way here. OSM has no name tag.

projects.notes: This is a DESC-Duke Energy Carolinas interconnection (tie lines), which matters for the coordination context. Dominion's page (desc-saluda-bushriver-page) says the work replaces 15 miles of 115 kV steel lattice towers with steel poles (SPDC) between Ballentine and Little Mountain. Construction runs summer 2026 to March 2027; the SCRTP in-service date is 12/31/2026. The full Saluda Hydro-Bush River path is about 52 km (33 mi), so the endpoint midpoint (about 34.153,-81.433) falls in the Chapin/Little Mountain part of the work corridor.

endpoints.validation: The name and 230/115 kV voltage match, and it is in West Ashley, Charleston. It matches the Church Creek Substation box on Dominion's route map (church-creek-charleston-map.jpg, linked from the cached desc-church-creek-charleston-page).

endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/229031773 power=substation voltage=115000 (unnamed). HIFLD 112634 (SCE&G 115 kV, 4.0 km) runs from Faber Place along Azalea Dr and ends at this feature (32.84532,-79.97412).

issuesFixed: desc:6870 A Bush River: FALSE MATCH fixed. The researcher chose an unnamed DESC 230/115 kV sub in West Columbia (OSM way/544217903, 34.01969,-81.12803). The terminal is actually Duke Energy Carolinas' Bush River Tie near Newberry: OSM way/185168619 (230/100/44 kV) = HIFLD node 116988, at 34.25232,-81.64903. Evidence: the FSAR tie table ('Saluda Hydro #1/#2 – Bush River (B)/(W) 115', listed under Duke Energy-Carolinas); SERTP 2025 'Bush River Tie' 115/100 kV autotransformers and Bush River Tie – Buzzard Roost 100 kV line, which HIFLD 126116 confirms; and a new cached Dominion Saluda-Bush River page (Ballentine to Little Mountain; Lexington, Newberry and Richland counties; 15 miles). The endpoint moved 54.5 km and the project center moved 27 km. Changed to confirmed; the notes now call it a DESC-Duke tie, give the 15-mile scope and the summer 2026 to March 2027 construction window, and drop the wrong '6-mile' reading.

desc:6853 B-F: the researcher listed 3 endpoints for a substation project (VCS1 and Killian after Scout). lib/matching/geo.ts centerOf() averages the first two endpoints, so the center would have been the Scout-VCS1 midpoint, 14.4 km from Scout. VCS1 and Killian now appear only in the notes, and Scout is the single site, as the schema requires.

desc:6853 B-F Scout point moved 2.2 km, from 34.1876,-80.98155 (the end of the rail spur, which sits on I-77 and is only 1.4 km from the VCS1-Killian line) to 34.19,-81.005, inside the Scout tract west of I-77 and south of Blythewood Road. PSC Order 2024-357 describes about 2.5 miles of new right-of-way running west across I-77. Kept as locality, 3000 m, lower-confidence.
desc:6853 B-F Killian (now in the notes) independently confirmed: the HIFLD Wateree-Killian 230 kV path totals 34.5 mi, against SCRTP 6808 R's 'Length - 35 miles'.

desc:6381: the researcher listed 3 endpoints for a substation project (Flat Rock locality, Belvedere Sw Sta, Graniteville). centerOf() would have averaged Flat Rock with Belvedere, pulling the center 4 km toward North Augusta and Georgia, even though no work is stated at either tapped-line terminal.
